title: finite model on immersion range
statement:
theorem finite_model_on_immersion_range
    (Λ Ω : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1})
    [MonObj Λ] [MonObj Ω] [IsCommMonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Ω]
    (a : Λ ⟶ Ω) [IsMonHom a] {T V : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : V ⟶ T) [IsImmersion f]
    (M : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Ω T))
    (P : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology V) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ V))
    (hP : IsLocallyFinitelyPresented (condensedRingObj Λ V) P)
    (e : (Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap a V)).obj P ≅
      (CondensedRing.upperStar Ω f).obj M)
    {U : Scheme.{u}} (g : U ⟶ T) (hr : Set.range g ⊆ Set.range f) :
    ∃ (Q : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ U)),
      IsLocallyFinitelyPresented (condensedRingObj Λ U) Q ∧
      Nonempty ((Mod.extendScalars (coefficientMap a U)).obj Q ≅
        (CondensedRing.upperStar Ω g).obj M). This is the exact Lean statement, with the definitions cited in stmt_deps.

source.place: Tags 09AA, 09AH, 09AB; closed support and topological invariance

proof.text: Construct a pullback square of f along g and eliminate its scheme-and-morphism witnesses as abstract data. Range containment makes the second projection surjective. It is an immersion by base change, hence a closed immersion because its image is all of U.
Pull P back along the first projection and push it forward along the second. These operations preserve local finite presentation.

On the pullback, pullIso commutes scalar extension with inverse image. The counit, the given model isomorphism, and upperStarComp around the cartesian square give an isomorphism after pulling back along the second projection. Its inverse image is fully faithful, so lift this isomorphism to U.

mathlib_searches.query: A pro-etale cover of a surjective closed subscheme has a refinement pulled back from a pro-etale cover of the ambient scheme
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits about etale pretopologies, etale morphisms and surjective singleton covers; no pro-etale closed-immersion model or covering-refinement theorem. The source library affine ind-etale closed-site lift supplies the missing geometry.
Twelve hits, including Surjective.of_comp and stability and iso instances. These support the geometric arguments but do not state finite-model transport or pro-etale cover lifting.

Twenty-five hits, including closed embeddings on prime spectra and the fact that a surjective closed immersion into a reduced scheme is an isomorphism. No pro-etale covering or module-presentation result.

mathlib_searches.query: A surjective closed immersion induces an equivalence on module sheaves on the pro-etale site, preserving locally finite presentation and finite coefficient models under restriction

No exact pro-etale module or support-induction theorem.
